title: Disaster Recovery Patterns: RTO, RPO & Multi-Region Strategies — D6
purpose: Shows the documented internals needed to predict behavior; undocumented details are observed behavior and may change.
routing_rationale: Selecting a Disaster Recovery strategy requires balancing the financial cost of idle standby infrastructure against the business revenue loss per hour of operational downtime.

nodes.label: Cloud SQL Primary DB
nodes.detail: Primary transactional database writing WAL logs.

nodes.label: Cross-Region Read Replica
nodes.detail: Replicates WAL changes across Google global backbone with RPO < 5 seconds.

nodes.label: Warm Standby GKE Cluster
nodes.detail: Keeps core pods pre-warmed; ready to autoscale to 100 pods within 3 minutes.

nodes.label: Promotable Secondary DB
nodes.detail: Promoted to read-write primary upon regional failover activation.

steps.title: Asynchronous Cross-Region Sync
steps.action: Primary writes replicate across Google dedicated fiber backbone to us-east4.
steps.why_traversal: Guarantees RPO < 5 seconds without penalizing primary write latency.

steps.title: Warm Standby Ready State
steps.action: Standby GKE cluster runs minimal baseline instances, ready for instant scale-up.
steps.why_traversal: Reduces RTO to < 5 minutes while saving 70% compute costs compared to hot standby.

scenarios.label: Cold Backup RTO Disaster
scenarios.root_cause: Organization used Cold Backup strategy for 20TB database to save money.
scenarios.diverted_path: Restoring 20TB database from GCS bucket took 28 hours during regional outage.
scenarios.blast_radius: Business offline for over a full day; massive financial loss.
scenarios.recovery: Upgrade mission-critical workloads from Cold Backup to Warm Standby or Spanner Multi-Region.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted

scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
